Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Printing Materials for printing (soil, ash, charcoal dust, chalk dust, paper, feathers, grass), part of MYSELF THEME: MYSELF Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Lear in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we make hand prints? 2. How do we make hand prints?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Printing Materials for printing (soil, ash, charcoal dust, chalk dust, paper, feathers, grass) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: Learner displays confidence in talking or signing about clothes worn by family members.

● Communication and collaboration: Learner speaks or signs about clothes worn by family members while collaborating with

others.

Values:
● Love: Learner portrays a caring attitude by sharing materials with peers as they carry out their work.

● Responsibility: Learner distributes materials amongst themselves, store their work well and clear working areas.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life Skills; Learners develop life skills of self-awareness while appreciating their own hand or foot prints.

Link to other learning areas:

Environmental activities; Learners keep the environment clean by improvising printing materials and clearing the working area.

Suggested learning resources.

Soil, Ash, Charcoal, Dust, Chalk, Papers, Feathers, Grass, Hearing aids.
